text:
Connor Brown has 13 points in 17 games and his ice time has climbed to 17.6 minutes a night over his last ten, almost four more than his season average. New Jersey keeps handing him a bigger role, and he keeps answering: a goal and an assist in the 3-2 win over Columbus on Nov. 23, including the winner.

The finishing is the part to be careful with. He has 7 goals on 4.0 expected (the quality of his chances, in goals), and he is scoring on 26% of his shots against 16% last season. Our range for his true rate runs 12.5% to 17.6%. The Devils have also scored 4.5 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Something has to give.

What holds up is the playmaking. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 19% of his setups going across the royal road last season against 7% for a typical forward, the pass that moves a goalie side to side. At 32, on his fifth NHL team, Brown is earning big minutes. He just won't keep scoring on a quarter of his shots.
headline: Brown is shooting 26%, and the Devils need it
